title: Held-out benefit of validated exploration lessons
hypothesis: On held-out comparable coding tasks, conditionally promoted lessons outperform an unfiltered exploration ledger in correctness-preserving efficiency.
falsified_if: D repeatedly loses correctness or shows no meaningful advantage over C; persuasive blind agreement without held-out gains is not confirmation.
deterministic_outcomes: disjoint discovery, validation and evaluation tasks
recorded independent interpretation agreement, not a promotion gate
efficiency_outcomes: amortized discovery and validation cost reported separately
decision_rule: Requires a real frozen promotion-v1 corpus with matched raw and distilled evidence; absent corpus or no promoted lessons blocks execution. Register each conditional candidate and five distinct validation tasks before results. Freeze the full ledger before held-out testing; do not feed smoke or pilot outcomes back into it. Run 8 smoke cases (simple_prompt plus existing_codebase_edit, four arms), then 36 randomized pilot cases (3 scenarios, 3 reps, 4 arms), at most 44 launches with a $10 between-run estimate threshold and 3600 active seconds. Primary contrast D versus C; A/B secondary. Continue only with no additional observed correctness losses and at least 15% lower aggregate cost or median wall time, without >10% regression in the other metric. With three reps this is a directional pilot, not statistical approval; mixed outcomes are inconclusive. Blind interpretation reviews must be separate fresh instances with tools disabled, seeing measurements/interventions only; agreement is triangulation, not independent task validation. A fixture clone or repetition is not a distinct validation task. The initial short scenarios do not establish long-task benefit. Cohort appropriateness must be reviewed before creating the real corpus.
